## 1. Configuration options and order of operations

### 1.1 Discovery activation and methods

After activating the Discovery application, there are two options to get started:
- **Agentless discovery**
- **Agent-based discovery**

Source: [Quick Start Guide for Discovery - ServiceNow Community](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-articles/quick-start-guide-for-discovery/ta-p/3408613)

### 1.2 MID Server configuration

The MID Server (Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery Server) facilitates communication and data exchange between the ServiceNow instance and the client's environment. Key configuration considerations include:
- Number of MID Servers needed
- Number of servers, network devices, and data centers to support
- Geographies to be covered
- Data sources to integrate
- Cloud vendor infrastructure to support
- MID Server sizing (CPU, memory considerations for patterns producing large payloads such as Kubernetes, Cloud Discovery, or certain application patterns)
- MID Server Load Balancing or Failover clusters for Discovery Schedules with strict networking requirements

Sources:
- [Discovery and MID Server Resources - ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0540193)
- [MID Server Sizing for Discovery - ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB2729323)
- [Solved: MID server configuration - ServiceNow Community](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-forum/mid-server-configuration/m-p/2762368)

> UNVERIFIED: The research did not return an exhaustive list of specific `discovery.properties` system properties or all individual configuration properties. The evidence covers high-level implementation options and MID Server configuration considerations rather than a complete property reference.

### 1.3 Order of operations (Discovery processing phases)

When a device is discovered, Discovery processing happens in the following sequence:

**Phase 1 — Scanning (Port Scan)**
The Shazzam probe scans TCP and UDP IP ports to determine which ports are open and attempts to get a response from open ports.
Source: [Troubleshooting the Classification Phase in Discovery - ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0535236)

**Phase 2 — Classification**
Begins right after the Shazzam port scanner probe and ends after processing those results, triggering the Identification phase. Based on the open ports, Discovery looks up the Port Probe table to determine what type of Classify probe needs to be launched. Each classification type dictates the probes that Discovery runs for the Identification and Exploration phases.

Base-system classification priority order: **WMI > SSH > SNMP > CIM**
Sources:
- [Troubleshooting the Classification Phase in Discovery - ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0535236)
- [Understand Phases of Discovery - ServiceNow Community](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-articles/understand-phases-of-discovery/ta-p/3116984)
- [What are the phases on the Discovery? - ServiceNow Community](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-forum/what-are-the-phases-on-the-discovery/m-p/2863593)

**Phase 3 — Identification**
Triggered after classification completes. The classification results determine which identification probes are launched.

**Phase 4 — Exploration**
CI Classification triggers the initial probes launched during this phase. All exploration probes that meet the relevant conditions are triggered after the identification probe. This phase collects in-depth information about the device and its relationships.
Source: [Troubleshooting the Exploration Phase in Discovery - ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0535240)

**Important credential note:** A credential that is successful during Classification and Identification does not imply that it is successful during Exploration. Most probes use the same credentials used during Classification and Identification, however some probes have additional requirements.
Source: [Troubleshooting the Exploration Phase in Discovery - ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0535240)

## 2. CI Class Manager — key bread crumbs

CI Class Manager is the central location for configuring Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) rules and settings. To access it, navigate to **Configuration > CI Class Manager**.
Source: [ServiceNow KB1064718 — CMDB Identification and Reconciliation Engine fundamentals](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB1064718)

| Setting | What it controls | Interface location |
|---|---|---|
| Identification Rules | How Discovery matches/identifies CIs (e.g., by serial number, name, MAC address) | CI Class Manager > your CI class > **Identification Rule** tab |
| Inclusion Rules (Advanced) | Which CIs are taken into consideration for identification (e.g., only Operational status) | CI Class Manager > your CI class > **Inclusion Rule (Advanced)** tab |
| Reconciliation Rules | Which data sources are allowed to update CI attributes, and their priority | CI Class Manager > your CI class > **Reconciliation Rules** tab |

Sources:
- [ServiceNow Community — A Deep Dive into CI Class Manager and IRE](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-forum/a-deep-dive-into-ci-class-manager-and-ire-servicenow-cmdb/m-p/3486406)
- [ServiceNow Community — CMDB identification and reconciliation discussion](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-forum/need-help-in-cmdb-ci-class-expansion/td-p/3575528)

Identification Rule tab details:
- **Identifier Entries** — choose attributes from the main table, a lookup table, or a combination to uniquely identify CIs
- **Priority** and **Criterion Attributes** for each identifier entry
Source: [ServiceNow Community — A Deep Dive into CI Class Manager and IRE](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-forum/a-deep-dive-into-ci-class-manager-and-ire-servicenow-cmdb/m-p/3486406)

## 3. Preventing duplicates; insert vs update in the CMDB

### Core mechanism: Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)

ServiceNow uses the **Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)** as a centralized framework to decide whether an incoming CI payload should **update an existing CI** or **insert a new CI** into the CMDB. The IRE handles both creation of new CIs and updates to existing ones, and helps maintain CMDB integrity when multiple data sources feed configuration data.
Source: [ServiceNow KB1064718 — CMDB Identification and Reconciliation Engine fundamentals](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB1064718)

### 3.1 Identification Rules (the update-vs-insert decision)

Identification Rules are the primary control for determining whether a CI already exists. When a new CI is introduced, the IRE checks the CI Identification Rules for that CI class:
- **If a match is found** → ServiceNow updates the existing CI record with the new information.
- **If no match is found** → a new CI record is created in the appropriate CI class.

Source: [ServiceNow Community — Elevating CMDB data quality with well-defined CI identification](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/elevating-cmdb-data-quality-with-well-defined-ci-identification/ta-p/2857355)

How to configure them:
- Go to **Configuration > CI Class Manager** to see and edit the identification rules that apply to a specific CI class.
  Source: [ServiceNow KB0869861](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0869861)
- Ensure **strong identifiers** (for example, Serial Number + Manufacturer, or Name + IP/MAC combinations) are consistently configured for related classes.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — How to avoid duplicate CI creation](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-forum/how-to-avoid-duplicate-ci-creation/m-p/3498456)
- Identification rules can be priority-based and hierarchical—for example, first check Serial Number, then Name, then IP Address + MAC Address. They can also reference related lists (such as IP Address tables).
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — Identification and Reconciliation rules versus coalesce](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-forum/identification-and-reconciliation-rules-versus-coalesce/m-p/986797)
- **Inclusion rules** can narrow which CIs are included in the identification process (e.g., only CIs with Operational Status = Operational). However, inclusion rules can lead to duplicate CIs if not configured properly.
  Source: [ServiceNow KB1064718](https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB1064718); [ServiceNow Community — Elevating CMDB data quality](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/elevating-cmdb-data-quality-with-well-defined-ci-identification/ta-p/2857355)

Important caveat: Duplicate CIs are identified **in real-time as data is processed by the IRE**, not by a separate daily job. If data is inserted into `cmdb_ci` without going through the IRE (for example, via GlideRecord or the REST API Explorer), the identification rules are bypassed and duplicates can still be created.
Source: [ServiceNow Community — Duplicate Configuration Items in the ServiceNow CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/community/in-other-news/duplicate-configuration-items-in-the-servicenow-cmdb/ba-p/2271418)

### 3.2 Reconciliation Rules (control which sources may update)

While Identification Rules answer "Does this CI already exist?", Reconciliation Rules answer "Which data source is allowed to update this CI or its attributes?"
Source: [ServiceNow Community — CMDB understanding identification and reconciliation rules](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/cmdb-understanding-identification-and-reconciliation-rules-and/ta-p/3520826)

- Reconciliation rules specify which data sources can update a table or a set of table attributes, and they can be defined at the parent and/or child class level.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — CMDB Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/cmdb-identification-reconciliation/ta-p/2301712)
- Best practice: ensure there is a reconciliation rule in place for **each data source authorized to update CIs** in the CMDB.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — CMDB Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/cmdb-identification-reconciliation/ta-p/2301712)
- Together, Identification and Reconciliation rules help prevent duplication, reconcile CI attributes, reclassify CIs, and allow only authoritative data sources to update CI records.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — CMDB Identification and Reconciliation](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-articles/cmdb-identification-reconciliation/ta-p/2301712)

### 3.3 Route every data source through the IRE (best practice)

To avoid duplicates, route all CMDB population through the IRE:
- **Discovery**: Use IRE for Discovery data so CIs are matched against existing records before insertion.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — How to avoid duplicate CI creation](https://www.servicenow.com/community/cmdb-forum/how-to-avoid-duplicate-ci-creation/m-p/3498456)
- **Import Sets / Transform Maps**: Use Identification and Reconciliation for import sets as well.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — Identification and Reconciliation rules versus coalesce](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-forum/identification-and-reconciliation-rules-versus-coalesce/m-p/986797)
- **Service Graph Connectors**: Rely on the IRE's priority-based matching system rather than traditional coalesce fields.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — How to verify identification rules for Service Graph Connectors](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-articles/how-to-verify-identification-rules-for-service-graph-connectors/ta-p/3417132)
- **REST API / direct inserts**: Avoid inserting CIs via GlideRecord or raw REST API calls outside the IRE, because those mechanisms do not check identification rules.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — Duplicate Configuration Items in the ServiceNow CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/community/in-other-news/duplicate-configuration-items-in-the-servicenow-cmdb/ba-p/2271418)

### 3.4 Coalesce fields (simpler, legacy alternative)

In transform maps, a **coalesce field** can be used to match on a single unique field (e.g., Serial Number) to decide update vs. insert. However, Identification and Reconciliation rules are more powerful because they support complex, multi-criteria, priority-based matching across related tables. For CMDB data, the IRE is strongly recommended over relying solely on coalesce fields.
Source: [ServiceNow Community — Identification and Reconciliation rules versus coalesce](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-forum/identification-and-reconciliation-rules-versus-coalesce/m-p/986797)

### 3.5 Detect and remediate existing duplicates

- The **CMDB Health Dashboard** runs a scheduled job called **Correctness Score Calculation** (available under CMDB Health Preferences). It scans `cmdb_ci` records against their class's CI Identification Rules; records identified as duplicates are assigned to a de-duplication task and marked as "duplicate".
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — Duplicate Configuration Items in the ServiceNow CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/community/in-other-news/duplicate-configuration-items-in-the-servicenow-cmdb/ba-p/2271418)
- Starting with the **New York release**, the `cmdb_ci` table includes a **Duplicate Of** field. When the IRE inserts a CI detected as a duplicate of two or more existing CIs, the duplicate CI references the earliest-created CI in this field.
  Source: [ServiceNow Community — Duplicate Configuration Items in the ServiceNow CMDB](https://www.servicenow.com/community/in-other-news/duplicate-configuration-items-in-the-servicenow-cmdb/ba-p/2271418)

### Summary checklist

| Goal | Configuration action |
|---|---|
| Prevent duplicate CIs | Define strong, consistent Identification Rules per CI class in CI Class Manager; route all sources through IRE |
| Update existing CI instead of inserting | Ensure incoming data matches an active Identification Rule; use Reconciliation Rules to authorize the updating source |
| Control which source wins | Set up Reconciliation Rules per data source and attribute |
| Catch duplicates already in CMDB | Run CMDB Health / Correctness Score Calculation; review de-duplication tasks and the Duplicate Of field |

**Key sources:** ServiceNow KB0869861, KB1064718; ServiceNow Community articles on CI Identification Rules, CMDB Identification & Reconciliation, and duplicate CI identification.
